# PositronicKit

> A Swift toolkit for building AI agents: transport-neutral runtime orchestration (turn loop, threads, tool routing), a structured prompt composition DSL, and the shared contracts that tie them together — without imposing a specific networking or hosting model.

PositronicKit follows semver for tagged releases beginning with `1.0.0`. The core modules (`PositronicKit`, `PKPrompt`, `PKContracts`) and the provider adapters are verified on Apple platforms and Linux; `PKLocalEmbeddings` is verified on Apple default, Linux, and Apple MiniLM trait paths. Add it as a Swift Package dependency and import only the modules you need — see the Quick Start below before writing any code against it.

## Getting Started

- [README: Quick Start](README.md#quick-start): add the package dependency, import the modules you need, and use `kit.model`, `kit.threads`, `kit.agents`, and `kit.workspaces` as the supported capability entry points.
- [Setup Guide](docs/Setup.md): choosing an entry point, facade configuration (minimal vs. production), default tool installation, provider registration, logging, and errors.
- [Development Guide](docs/Development.md): contributor platform setup, Podman gates, focused tests, MiniLM assets, and bridge checks.
- [Context Map](CONTEXT-MAP.md): v4 vocabulary ownership and relationships between runtime, prompting, and contracts.
- [Architecture Decisions](docs/adr/): accepted v4 domain, dependency, durability, Workspace, and execution decisions.
- [PositronicKitExamples](Sources/PositronicKitExamples): runnable examples that double as living documentation — read `main.swift`, `PositronicKitUsageExamples.swift`, and `PKPromptExamples.swift` before inventing your own composition pattern.

## Core Concepts

- [Usage Guide](docs/Usage.md): current tagged-release usage, initialization and execution, tool outputs, and local embeddings.
- [Architecture](docs/Architecture.md): capability values, context/state management, turn execution flow, and the v1 extension point registry. Concrete managers, task registries, and pipeline stages are facade implementation details.
- [Runtime customization](docs/Usage.md#agent-persistence): the four bounded roles in `RuntimeCustomization`, including required/optional context contributions and post-terminal sink behavior.
- [Prompt Composition](docs/PKPromptComposition.md): the `@PromptBuilder` DSL, assembly/rendering, cache policies, and `PromptJournal` stable-prefix journaling.
- [Sidecar Directives](docs/SidecarDirectives.md): piggy-backed auxiliary generations (titles, tags, summaries) riding the same LLM request as the user-visible response.

## Providers

- [Setup Guide: Provider Registration](docs/Setup.md#provider-registration): register a concrete provider (`PKOpenAIProvider`, `PKOpenRouterProvider`, `PKOllamaProvider`, `PKAnthropicProvider`, `PKFoundationModelsProvider`) before constructing an `LLMService` from configuration.
- [Usage Guide: Local Embeddings](docs/Usage.md#4-local-embeddings): `PKLocalEmbeddings`/`LocalEmbeddingService` — Natural Language by default on Apple, MiniLM on Linux, opt-in Apple MiniLM via the `MiniLMEmbeddings` trait; re-embed when moving content across backends or platforms.

## Reference

- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): breaking changes to public surfaces are called out under a `Breaking` heading — check before upgrading a pinned version.
- [Releasing](docs/Releasing.md): the release workflow, tagging steps, and downstream upgrade cadence.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): source-of-truth hierarchy, v4 convergence constraints, contribution workflow, and build/test/verify commands. Written for coding agents contributing *to* this package, not for agents consuming it at runtime.

## Optional

- [README: Verification](README.md#verification): `make verify` / `verify-products` / `verify-minilm` / Linux gates, useful if you're vendoring or patching the package rather than just consuming its public API.
